transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-11-15
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 55 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Alex Rivera (Zenith Partner PM), Priya Desai (Zenith SE), Mark Holloway (Zenith Marketplace Ops)

[00:00] Maya Chen: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh, really appreciate you carving out time. Quick intro, I'm Maya, I'll own the partner motion on the Redwood side, and Daniel is our systems engineer.
[00:15] Alex Rivera: Thanks Maya, Alex here, excited to sync. Quick context ZenithCloud wants to list a Redwood-managed integration in our marketplace and bundle a joint solution offering. We're looking at listing, reference arch, and what we need for submission.
[00:30] Daniel Ortiz: Cool, thanks. On Redwood's side we'll want to walk through the listing metadata, the deployment artifacts ee.g. Terraform snippets or a Marketplace-aware helm chart and any reference arch docs you want to show. Also curious about billing flow, SSO, and data residency constraints.
[00:45] Priya Desai: Yeah, for compliance we need to make sure SOC2 and encryption details are documented. Also, how the private deployments would work if a customer wants VPC-only.
[01:00] Mark Holloway: From the ops side we care about the container images and verification process, like how you sign images, and the size of the artifacts. We have limits on large disk images in the marketplace portal.
[01:15] Daniel Ortiz: Understood. So a couple of quick notes Redwood supports hosted, dedicated, and private. For marketplace listing we typically provide two options: a hosted integration (we host, marketplace charges via our billing) and a private deploy reference (customer deploys via Terraform into their account). For the latter we supply IaC modules and reference arch.
[01:35] Alex Rivera: That matches what I'd expect. On the marketplace listing itself we need the tile, short/long descriptions, logo assets, and the pricing model. Do you have standard pricing templates?
[01:50] Maya Chen: We can share recommended pricing tiers per-token tiers for hosted and reserved capacity SKU for dedicated. I'll attach an example. Heads-up, sometimes our docs reference Redwood Dedicate um, sorry Redwood Dedicated, transcription note we've seen it mis-typed in older docs.
[02:05] Priya Desai: (laughs) yeah the docs sometimes call it Redwood dedicate, we noticed. Important to clarify the SLA and upgrade path.
[02:20] Daniel Ortiz: On the technical side, for the private deployment we bundle: a Terraform module for provisioning GPUs/VMs, a helm chart for the runtime, and example config with KV cache options and quantization profiles. We'll provide a sample Docker/OCI image reference, but in many marketplaces you ask vendors to host images in the partner registry or provide a digest.
[02:40] Mark Holloway: How big are the images typically and can they be split? Our portal complains if an image is >2GB.
[02:50] Daniel Ortiz: The runtime base tends to be 1.2-1.8GB compressed for the inference container, plus model artifacts which we usually pull from a model store. For marketplace we recommend hosting the model artifacts externally (S3 or cloud storage) and reference them in the helm/Terraform spec so the install fetches at deploy time.
[03:10] Alex Rivera: For the joint solution, we also want a reference architecture diagram that shows flow: User -> Zenith Marketplace -> Redwood Hosted endpoint / or customer VPC deployment -> model inference -> telemetry to Redwood Console + Zenith monitoring.
[03:30] Maya Chen: We'll produce that diagram. Also important: for the hosted path we need to provide a single-sign-on experience for marketplace customers OAuth/OIDC integration and optional SAML for enterprises.
[03:45] Priya Desai: Do you support SAML? We have enterprises that require IdP-initiated flows.
[03:55] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, Redwood supports SAML and OIDC; we have a docs page that outlines SSO setup and metadata exchange. We'll include the SAML metadata file in the marketplace bundle.
[04:10] Alex Rivera: On billing, how does charge reconciliation work for reserved capacity? We want to display pricing in our portal but customers expect a single invoice.
[04:25] Maya Chen: For reserved capacity we do monthly invoices to the customer; for marketplace billing we can either route via the marketplace billing (if your platform supports vendor payouts) or bill directly to the customer and provide usage metrics for reconciliation. We should check Zenith's marketplace payout model.
[04:45] Mark Holloway: We do vendor payouts but need proper SKU mapping. We'll need a small mapping table and sample SKUs.
[04:55] Maya Chen: We'll provide SKU naming suggestions and a sample CSV for SKU mapping.
[05:05] Priya Desai: Security artifacts: can you share SOC2 report, encryption at rest details, KMS/HSM integration notes? Our procurement will ask.
[05:20] Daniel Ortiz: Yes, we have SOC2 Type II and we support customer-managed keys via KMS in private deploys; for hosted we have envelope encryption and optional customer KMS integration we'll include the security pack.
[05:35] Alex Rivera: Great. Next, we need a test plan for the dev org deploy. Steps: 1) create staging account, 2) deploy Terraform module, 3) run smoke tests (latency, throughput, auth), 4) validate billing and user provisioning.
[05:55] Daniel Ortiz: That sounds right. For smoke tests we'll provide a sample postman collection and a small load script that runs 50 concurrent requests to verify autoscaling and KV cache warmup. Note: our runtime uses KV cache that sometimes is transcribed as KV cash in older transcripts.
[06:15] Alex Rivera: (laughs) good to know. For the marketplace submission workflow, what's the typical lead time? From listing submission to approval?
[06:25] Maya Chen: It depends on the marketplace usually 1-3 weeks for review if all artifacts are present; longer if security/compliance reviews are required. We'll aim to have everything in your hands within 3 business days after this call for a first pass.
[06:40] Priya Desai: On the reference architecture doc, can you add sample metrics we expect to emit to Redwood Console and to Zenith monitoring? Like token-per-request, p95 latency, GPU utilization.
[06:55] Daniel Ortiz: Absolutely. We'll include telemetry keys, OpenTelemetry span names, and dashboards for p50/p95 latency, tokens/sec, and cost-per-token breakdown.
[07:10] Mark Holloway: Also, for marketplace artifact validation we need a signed manifest do you sign manifests?
[07:20] Daniel Ortiz: We sign images with cosign and can provide signed digests. We'll include instructions to verify signatures during your validation pipeline.
[07:30] Alex Rivera: Any gotchas for reference arch when a customer wants private air-gapped deploys?
[07:40] Daniel Ortiz: For air-gapped we provide an on-prem package and an offline installer; model artifacts need to be seeded into an internal bucket. There are additional licensing steps and support requirements; we can include an on-prem checklist.
[07:55] Maya Chen: Quick note from a sales/operator perspective, we recommend offering three listing SKUs: free trial (limited tokens), pay-as-you-go hosted, and dedicated/reserved for enterprise. That maps well to customer journeys.
[08:10] Alex Rivera: That helps. For co-marketing and joint solution brief we want a one-pager and a demo video. Can Redwood help with assets?
[08:20] Maya Chen: Yes, we can provide a co-branded one-pager, example screenshots from Redwood Console, and a short demo script. We'll ask marketing for the assets once we finalize the PRD.
[08:35] Priya Desai: Any integration tests we should run on our side for SAML/OIDC?
[08:45] Daniel Ortiz: We'll provide a checklist: metadata exchange, SP-initiated and IdP-initiated flows, attribute mapping for user roles, and test user provisioning flows.
[08:58] Alex Rivera: Are there any size or resource constraints for the dedicated deployment? We expect customers to want predictable latency and throughput.
[09:10] Daniel Ortiz: For Dedicated we recommend GPU instance pools; typical baseline for moderate workloads is 4 x A100-style GPUs in a pool with autoscaling. We provide guidance on batch size, kv-cache settings, sequence length. You'll get a performance profile from us post-benchmark.
[09:35] Mark Holloway: Speaking of benchmarks, can Redwood run a short benchmark using Zenith's sample dataset?
[09:45] Maya Chen: Yes, we can run an initial benchmark. We'll coordinate offline Daniel will need the dataset and expected SLA targets (p95 latency, throughput).
[09:58] Priya Desai: Any special network or firewall requirements for the private deployment?
[10:08] Daniel Ortiz: We'll provide a network diagram and recommended security groups, NAT, and egress requirements for fetching model artifacts and telemetry endpoints. If inside a restricted VPC, we'll support an outbound proxy or pre-seed artifacts.
[10:25] Alex Rivera: Cool. Anything else on the listing metadata legal terms, support SLAs, or trial length we need to document?
[10:35] Maya Chen: We'll provide an example SLA table and suggested trial 14-day credit. Legal terms we'll surface in the marketplace contract, but PR docs will include support window and contact info.
[10:50] Mark Holloway: One more ops item: can you provide a reinstall/upgrade path? Our customers want zero-downtime upgrades.
[11:00] Daniel Ortiz: Our helm charts support rolling updates and image digests; model updates can be canaried. We'll document upgrade procedures and recommended maintenance windows.
[11:15] Alex Rivera: Awesome. Quick recap then what are the action items?
[11:25] Maya Chen: Recap: Redwood to send marketplace checklist, pricing template, SKU csv, security pack (SOC2 etc.), and reference arch + Terraform snippets. Zenith to provide staging account and compliance requirements. Redwood and Zenith to schedule a demo in staging once Terraform/helm artifacts are ready.
[11:45] Priya Desai: That aligns. We'll aim to have the compliance list over by Friday.
[11:52] Daniel Ortiz: I'll start packaging the Terraform module and snippets and drop them in a sandbox repo.
[11:58] Alex Rivera: Cool, I'll send a calendar invite for the follow-up deploy week of Nov 22.

End of transcript.

Follow-up notes: deliverables expected in the next 3-5 business days from Redwood, follow-up deploy scheduled, and joint solution PRD kickoff.
